Issued at 1023 PM CST Sun Nov 1 2026

Earlier this Sunday evening there was already a line of 
thunderstorms occurring ahead of an short wave trough which was 
preceding the main, stronger, upper level trough currently 
crossing the four corners areas. Models have not changed much 
over the past 24 hours with the first upper wave crossing 
southwest Kansas overnight with the main upper low then moving 
across western Kansas on late Monday/Monday night and deepening.
This will result in two opportunities for thunderstorms, 
(overnight and again late Monday/Monday night) a few storms may 
be strong or severe. The better opportunity for severe 
thunderstorms will be late Monday when the main upper level 
trough begins to cross western Kansas. Very windy conditions 
will also be possible as this upper level trough crosses western
Kansas which will initially result in highs in the 70 due to 
the potential for deep mixing which will allow unseasonably warm
ahead of approaching cold front mixing down to the surface. 
This will then be followed by a strong cold front late Monday as
gusty northwest winds usher colder air into the area Monday 
night and Tuesday. This colder air mass settling into southwest 
Kansas on Tuesday combined with clouds and lingering 
precipitation will result in highs Tuesday afternoon only in the
50s. Combine this with possible wind gusts in excess of 45 mph 
then wind chills may struggle to get much higher the mid 40s 
Tuesday afternoon. 

Marginal risk for isolated wind gusts in excess of 50 mph late 
tonight For late tonight...An upper level short wave trough 
will precede the main upper level trough and move across 
southwest Kansas overnight. Ahead of this initial upper wave a 
line of thunderstorms had already developed across southeast 
Colorado and New Mexico and as of 04z was approaching southwest
Kansas. Models are in good agreement with this line of 
thunderstorms moving east/northeast across southwest Kansas 
overnight as the upper level trough passes. Main risk from a few
of the stronger storms will be wind gusts greater than 50 mph given
forecast downdraft capes. 

A slight chance for severe thunderstorms capable of producing 
strong gusty winds and hail being possible Monday afternoon.
On Monday...A brief break in the precipitation will occur 
across southwest Kansas early in the day an our initial upper 
wave exits the area and the primary upper level trough moves 
across the Rockies and out into the West Central High Plains. 
Increasing southerly winds ahead will draw higher moisture back 
into southwest Kansas as a strong cold front moves across 
southwest Kansas and another surface boundary remains nearly 
stationary east of highway 283. As this cold front over takes 
the other surface boundary late day the low level 
forcing/moisture convergence will improve along the boundary 
east of highway 183 which will allow scattered thunderstorms to 
develop (increasing from <10% to near 40% after 21z) given 
improving synoptic upper level lift ahead of the upper trough 
and 0-6km shear(>50knots). Early in this event there will be a 
risk of large hail with these storms given the potential for a 
few discrete supercells, however these storms is expected to 
then quickly become a line and surge east which favors strong 
gusty winds. The storm prediction center does mention the small 
chance for tornadoes across central Kansas with this line as it 
moves east late Monday but at this time the better tornado 
potential may end up being east of Pratt and Medicine Lodge and 
the low level shear improves due to the evening low level jet. 
We will be monitoring this area (Pratt/Medicine Lodge) closely 
after 5pm but at this time it appears that any tornado risk 
will be east of this area. These storms currently are expected
to move east of Pratt and Medicine Lodge by 7pm. Another area of
thunderstorms will be possible Monday night further west near 
the 500mb deformation zone at it moves across southwest Kansas.
Gusty winds will also accompany some of these storms but the 
severe weather risk will be low. 

Very windy and colder temperatures possible on Tuesday as the 
precipitation tapers off early in the day. A tight surface 
pressure gradient and 850mb winds of around 45 knots will spread
across southwest Kansas Monday night and continue on Tuesday as
a strong cold front crosses southwest Kansas on Monday.  This 
will easily supports the current NBM forecast with wind gusts 
around 40 mph range Monday night and Tuesday, however based on 
the forecast 850mb winds of along with the tight surface 
pressure gradient/cold air advection it appears even these gusty
winds may end up being be a little low. As a result would not 
be surprised if gusts end up in some areas as high as 45 to near
50 mph at times Tuesday afternoon as several of the BUFR 
soundings suggest via momentum transfer. This is also in around 
the 75th percentile. These gusty winds will usher our next shot
